Potassium permanganate can oxidize the amino group in aniline. In neutral conditions, this oxidation can lead to the formation of complex products. One of the known products of aniline oxidation is "aniline black," which is a complex polymer formed by the oxidation of aniline. This is different from nitrobenzene (which would require stronger oxidizing conditions and acid) or anilinium ion (which forms in acidic conditions).

Violaniline is another oxidation product of aniline, but aniline black is the more common product when using permanganate as an oxidizing agent in neutral conditions.

Based on my knowledge of organic chemistry, when aniline reacts with potassium permanganate in neutral solution, it forms aniline black, which is option A.
